newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit rangebound after overnight losses.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit rangebound after overnight losses.

text.p: Ringgit was rangebound, but sharply lower after heavy overnight losses caused by funds selling the Malaysian currency in London, dealers said.
They said some ringgit selling against the Singapore dollar and strong dollar/majors also affected sentiment.
Heavy dollar buying overnight in a relatively illiquid London market by U.S. and Japanese funds pulled down the ringgit below the 2.50 technical barrier.
"There was much activity around 2.5025 level. Covering by Singapore banks and KL commercial demand was well matched by profit-taking by London," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
They said the overnight selling and a strong dollar/majors had weakened sentiment for the ringgit in morning trading.
"Some funds sold around 100 (million) dollars (worth ringgit) in late London (yesterday). That much in London time had to move the market," a dealer with a Malaysian bank said.
Heavy ringgit selling against the Singapore dollar was also responsible for the Malaysian currency's decline, dealers said.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5028/31 per dollar against 2.4985/95 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5611/18 against0.5630/33.
